title: Why this chronicle matters now
summary: Zong-Liang Yang's research program continues to advance our understanding of land-atmosphere interactions, climate prediction, and extreme weather forecasting—fundamental questions with direct implications for climate change adaptation and societal resilience.

signals.label: Climate Prediction Research
signals.text: Yang's work on land surface modeling and climate prediction provides critical infrastructure for weather forecasting and climate change projections, with direct relevance to understanding extreme weather events and their impacts on society.

signals.label: Noah-MP Model Impact
signals.text: The Noah-MP model developed by Yang's team has become essential infrastructure used by NCAR, NOAA, and the National Water Model, enabling accurate weather prediction and climate forecasting worldwide.

signals.label: Extreme Weather Forecasting
signals.text: Yang's models proved critical in forecasting Hurricane Harvey's devastating impacts, demonstrating the real-world value of his research in protecting communities from extreme weather events and supporting emergency response planning.
